outcome: No proof, disproof, case settlement, or bound movement on Dickson's conjecture itself has been found since 26 January 2024; the conjecture remains open exactly as it was.
summary: Dickson's conjecture (1904) — that any admissible finite set of linear forms a_i + b_i·n is simultaneously prime for infinitely many n — remains completely open. It generalizes the twin prime conjecture (k=2) and Sophie Germain primes, and is itself a special case of Schinzel's Hypothesis H and equivalent to a restricted form of the Hardy-Littlewood prime k-tuples conjecture. The known partial results — Zhang (2013) proving bounded gaps between primes, Maynard and Tao (2013, independently) proving that admissible k-tuples of sufficient size contain infinitely many shifts with m primes for any fixed m, and Green-Tao-Ziegler's proof of the prime k-tuple conjecture for linear forms with no two satisfying a linear relation over the integers (giving infinitely many k-term prime arithmetic progressions) — all predate the 26 January 2024 window by roughly a decade, so none of them can count as an event in scope even under open_stale, since none of them settles the conjecture or a case of it in the first place (Green-Tao-Ziegler excludes exactly the parallel/coincident-form cases that make Dickson's conjecture hard, i.e. it proves a genuinely different, non-overlapping sufficient condition, not a case of Dickson's conjecture as literally stated for forms that can be linearly dependent). I searched arXiv listings, Google, and the current (2026) Wikipedia article on Dickson's conjecture directly — the live article's most recent citation is from 1996 and it contains no post-2024 status update. I also checked whether Dickson's conjecture appears as an AI target in the current wave of AI-driven Erdős-problem-solving (Google DeepMind's 'formal-conjectures' Lean benchmark, the OpenAI unit-distance-conjecture disproof, and reports of ~100 Erdős problems moved to 'solved' since October 2025). Dickson's conjecture is not among the Erdős problems being attacked; the only hit connecting it to that ecosystem is a GitHub issue (google-deepmind/formal-conjectures #5672) reporting a misformalization bug in a Lean *variant* of an unrelated problem (Erdos 891, 'variants.weisenberg'), where the formal statement omitted Dickson's conjecture as a required hypothesis for a different, conditional result. That bug (found by an 'AI-powered audit' per the fetched summary and fixed in PR #5771) is about the correctness of someone else's formalization that merely cites Dickson's conjecture as an assumption — it does not touch Dickson's conjecture's truth, forge a case of it, or move any bound on it, so it is out of scope under §3.1 (a related/citing context, not a case or resolution) and is not recorded as an event. No preprint, announcement, or repository posting anywhere claims progress on Dickson's conjecture itself in the window. The correct classification is open with no_change_found true.
competing_reading: One could argue the Green-Tao-Ziegler theorem (which does postdate Dickson's 1904 statement by a century but predates the 2024-01-26 window by ~18 years) is a 'case' of Dickson's conjecture already settled before the window and thus should be flagged as open_stale rather than plain open, since it does resolve the conjecture for a broad class of admissible forms (those with no two related by a rational affine dependency). I did not classify it that way because (a) it predates the window by so much that it was surely already reflected in the Wikipedia page's frozen 2024 wording, which still states the conjecture as fully open, and (b) more importantly, no new instance of this or a comparable case-settlement occurred inside the 2024-01-26–present window, so there is nothing to date as the 'first written argument' for an open_stale record — open_stale requires an event whose date needs recording, and the pre-existing, decade-old partial results don't constitute a discrete event in this window. If a reviewer wants the pre-window Green-Tao-Ziegler result explicitly logged, this record would become open_stale dated to 2006 (Green-Tao) / 2010s (Green-Tao-Ziegler) with the same no_change_found-in-window narrative in summary.
what_would_settle_it: A preprint or announcement, dated after 26 January 2024, that either (a) proves or disproves Dickson's conjecture in general, (b) proves it for some previously-unsettled class of admissible linear-form tuples not already covered by Green-Tao-Ziegler or Maynard-Tao, or (c) states a new quantitative bound specific to Dickson-type tuples (e.g. an improved density or size threshold for k in the 'infinitely many shifts with m primes' results) that a careful reading would say updates this bullet's text.
